nodes.name: domain.md
nodes.summary: Agent-workflow doc telling engineering skills how to consume the repo's domain documentation before exploring: read CONTEXT.md (or CONTEXT-MAP.md pointing at per-context CONTEXT.md files) and any relevant docs/adr/ entries, proceeding silently if they are absent. Shows single-context and multi-context directory layouts, requires using the glossary's vocabulary in agent output, and demands that output contradicting an existing ADR be flagged explicitly rather than silently overridden. The /domain-modeling skill (reached via /grill-with-docs and /improve-codebase-architecture) creates these docs lazily.

nodes.name: issue-tracker.md
nodes.summary: Defines GitHub as the repo's issue tracker, driven entirely through the gh CLI with concrete conventions for creating, reading, listing, commenting on, labelling, and closing issues, plus a flag (currently 'no') controlling whether external PRs act as a triage surface. Also documents the wayfinding operations used by /wayfinder: a wayfinder:map issue holding child tickets linked as GitHub sub-issues with native blocked_by dependencies, a frontier query that drops blocked or assigned children, and claim/resolve workflows.

nodes.name: triage-labels.md
nodes.summary: Maps the five canonical triage role names from mattpocock/skills to this repo's actual GitHub label strings: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, and wontfix, each with its meaning. Skills that mention a role apply the local label string from this table; the right-hand column is meant to be edited to match whatever vocabulary this repo actually uses.

edges.description: The tracker workflows in issue-tracker.md apply the canonical triage roles whose label strings are defined in triage-labels.md.
Triage labels are applied via the gh CLI issue workflows documented in issue-tracker.md.
